global.statement: With both coefficients free and positive sample mean, a finite MLE exists and is unique exactly when the variance with divisor $n$ exceeds the sample mean. Otherwise the Poisson supremum is unattained. With positive mean $\mu$ held and any positive count, the finite shape maximum exists and is unique exactly when $v+(\bar x-\mu)^2>\bar x$; equality also selects the unattained Poisson supremum. With positive shape held and any positive count, the mean maximum always exists and is unique. All-zero data with free shape attain the zero mass at $\lambda=0$, leaving a free mean unidentified; positive held shape instead gives an unattained mean-zero supremum. With $\lambda=0$ held only all-zero data are compatible, and a free mean is unidentified. Holding both coefficients leaves evaluation.
global.reason: At fixed $z=\sqrt{2\lambda+\lambda^2/\mu^2}$ the unique maximizing mean is $\bar x$. The Bessel-polynomial degree variance satisfies $V_k<E_k(k^2-E_k^2)/(k^2+E_k^2)$, proving strict shape-profile concavity in the compact coordinate $w$. Its inward Poisson score gives the existence criteria. The weaker bound $V_k\le E_k$ proves monotonicity and uniqueness of the held-shape mean score. The derivations and floating-point contract are given below.
